features.entity_name: Telescope Array central site, near Delta, Utah
features.method: Coordinate taken from the TA surface-detector array paper's own description of the site centre (39.3 N, 112.9 W, one-decimal-degree precision), fetched via the ar5iv HTML mirror. This is a description of the array itself, unlike the site record's current coordinate (a Nominatim geocode of the town of Delta, Utah, 60+ km away in places, precision_m 15000, explicitly documented there as 'NOT a survey point for the array') -- reported as a site coordinate correction candidate in the worklog. accuracy_m 6000 covers the one-decimal-degree rounding (+-0.05 degrees ~ 5.5 km at this latitude). The 507-station 1.2 km SD grid and the three fluorescence-detector sites (Black Rock Mesa, Long Ridge, Middle Drum) have widely repeated coordinates online, but every instance traces to a secondary/amateur-astronomy source (cleardarksky.com, itself Wikipedia's own citation for these values) rather than an official TA page or paper fetched this session, so they are not drawn (see worklog backlog).

summary.plain: The Telescope Array ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observatory near Delta, Utah: 507 surface-detector stations on a 1.2 km grid over ~700 km2, watched by three fluorescence-detector stations.
